title: Comprehensive EHMT1 variants analysis broadens genotype-phenotype associations and molecular mechanisms in Kleefstra syndrome

reviewer.method: Complete main-text reading using fresh pdftotext -layout; all four main figures and two main tables inspected as pixels; all 19 supplementary-PDF pages inspected as text and pixels; all 209 Table S2 rows across four sheets read as cell data. All 43 selected/alternate packets compared by exact patient ID and source row, without opening inference outputs during this review. This script transcribes those observations and explicit semantic qualifications, not autonomous evidence adjudication.

audit.exposure_note: Parent had seen aggregate compact-cohort outcomes before review. EHMT1 per-case inference ranks were not consulted during this source review. This is not a blinded or preregistered audit.

limitations: Source correspondence only. Authors’ LP/P classifications and episignatures are not independent clinical validation or raw laboratory reproduction.
Unknown/blank source fields cannot substantiate an explicitly absent phenotype. Broad organ-level negatives and category labels are qualified, not equivalent to detailed examinations.
The main article calls N-terminal truncations likely pathogenic, whereas Table S3 labels them pathogenic; preserve the disagreement.
Table S3 lists c.38_39insA as inherited from an affected parent, but main text and S2 row123 say de novo.
Supplementary family narratives and S2 disagree on ID/GDD/depression in some relatives; those conflicts are retained per phenotype.
Some S2 weight, psychiatric and additional-variant columns disagree with their free-text or other fields. Their clinical resolution requires source clarification.
Original benchmark cases, alternate selection, inference outputs and endpoints remain unchanged. No results were used to select which assertions to correct.
